# Rest exactly where the total stops falling

<!-- Generated by tools/research/registry.py; edit the matching JSON record. -->

`rest-exactly-where-falls-stop` · **recorded-checked** · theorem · F01 · [record](rest-exactly-where-falls-stop.json) · [register](../../../../RESULTS.md)

> Over any amounts, a balanced, dissipated family stops changing exactly where its total stops falling, and a world rests where its census total does. A least fall in Archimedean amounts or a finite reading gives this; along an amount falling at every step a world never rests.

<a id="laws--规律"></a>
## Laws

1. One premise: an amount's strict falls stop from T on, as far as can be refuted (it is not the case that after every step from T on a later strict fall stays unrefuted). Balanced and dissipated on from T on, a family's levels stop changing, as far as can be refuted, exactly where its total's strict falls stop: one way needs neither premise (across a strict fall of the total some member's level falls, as far as can be refuted), the other is the law of one step. (`Becoming.Amounts.FallsStop`, `Becoming.Amounts.fallsStop_congr`, `Becoming.Amounts.not_not_totalOf_le`, `Becoming.World.InAmounts.change_stops_iff`)
2. The rest theorem with that one premise: a world whose active relata lie from T on in one family, balanced and dissipated on, whose arising is embodied and whose family total stops falling rests from some step on, unrefuted; so does a world with a census of its active relata, all embodied, a balanced and dissipative flow and every step from T on enclosed, whose census's total stops falling, since across an enclosed step the census's total does not rise and falls strictly at each arising or ceasing. A total read off configurations a list holds stops falling. (`Becoming.World.InAmounts.rests_unrefuted_of_stops`, `Becoming.World.InAmounts.Enclosed.around_census`, `Becoming.World.InAmounts.census_still`, `Becoming.World.InAmounts.census_falls`, `Becoming.World.InAmounts.rests_unrefuted_enclosed_of_stops`, `Becoming.World.InAmounts.stops_of_reading`)
3. Amounts in which every amount not rising stops falling have no endless fall. A least fall (every strict fall by at least ε above nothing) in Archimedean amounts gives it, and whole numbers are the instance; in such amounts every world with a census, embodied, balanced, dissipative and enclosed from some step on rests. Each premise is needed: dyadic amounts are Archimedean with no least fall, layered amounts have a least fall and are not Archimedean, and in both some amount falls strictly at every step. (`Becoming.Amounts.NoEndlessFall`, `Becoming.Amounts.EndlessFall`, `Becoming.Amounts.FallsAtLeast`, `Becoming.Amounts.noEndlessFall_of_fallsAtLeast`, `Becoming.Amounts.whole_fallsAtLeast`, `Becoming.Amounts.whole_noEndlessFall`, `Becoming.Halving.falls_back`, `Becoming.Halving.endless`, `Becoming.Halving.no_least_fall`, `Becoming.Layered.endless`, `Becoming.Layered.fallsAtLeast`, `Becoming.World.InAmounts.rests_unrefuted_enclosed_of_noEndlessFall`)
4. Whole-number worlds are the instance with their own premises and nothing more: a finite world whose flow balances and dissipates and whose arising is embodied, and a counted world, embodied, balanced, dissipative and enclosed from some step on, rest, unrefuted, by the law over any amounts. (`Becoming.World.rests_unrefuted`, `Becoming.World.rests_unrefuted_enclosed`)
5. An endless fall keeps a world from rest: along any amount d falling strictly at every step, in any amounts, a standing passing between two relata (the holder at d t takes it all from itself and gives d (t + 1) to the other) has a census of its active relata, every relatum embodied, a balanced and dissipative flow and every step enclosed, and one relatum arises and the other ceases at every step; no list holds its levels. (`Becoming.Pass.amounts`, `Becoming.Pass.dissipative`, `Becoming.Pass.census`, `Becoming.Pass.embodied`, `Becoming.Pass.balanced`, `Becoming.Pass.enclosed`, `Becoming.Pass.never_rests`, `Becoming.Pass.endless_keeps_from_rest`, `Becoming.Pass.levels_unlisted`, `Becoming.Amounts.totalOf_single`)
6. Rest over every world in given amounts (every world with the enclosed premises rests) follows from no endless fall and leaves no amount falling at every step; so in dyadic and in layered amounts some world never rests, and in whole numbers every such world rests. (`Becoming.Amounts.WorldsRest`, `Becoming.Amounts.worldsRest_of_noEndlessFall`, `Becoming.Amounts.not_endlessFall_of_worldsRest`, `Becoming.Amounts.whole_worldsRest`, `Becoming.Halving.worlds_need_not_rest`, `Becoming.Layered.worlds_need_not_rest`)

<a id="conditions--条件"></a>
## Conditions

- No axiom. Amounts are any Amounts (a cancellative preordered commutative monoid with nothing least). Named where they enter: that the total's strict falls stop, balance with no amount made, dissipation read as whatever gives back all it takes takes nothing, embodiment, a census with enclosure from T on or one family covering activity; for the amounts, a least fall above nothing and the Archimedean property; for the converse, an amount falling strictly at every step. Equality of relata is not decided.

<a id="does-not-show--未表明"></a>
## Does not show

- That rest over every world in given amounts is, constructively, the absence of an endless fall: from an amount whose falls recur only as far as can be refuted, an amount falling at every step is not built without choosing the steps at which it falls; classically, with dependent choice, the conditions coincide.
- That the whole-number rest theorems are derived from the law over any amounts: they keep their own proofs below Becoming.InAmounts, which reads World; the instance shows their premises are exactly what the general law needs in whole numbers.
- That any physical system has a least fall or a finite reading: both are premises.
- How soon the world rests, or naming the step: that is a principle of omniscience (World.lpo_of_finite_ends).
- **Counterexample:** Pass.endless_keeps_from_rest: along any amount falling strictly at every step a standing passing between two relata meets every premise of the enclosed rest theorem but the stopping of the falls, and never rests; Halving.worlds_need_not_rest and Layered.worlds_need_not_rest: in dyadic amounts (no least fall) and in layered amounts (not Archimedean) some world never rests. [source](../../../../experiments/integrated-correction/general-framework/generative-basis/lean/becoming/Becoming/InAmounts.lean)

<a id="correspondence--对应"></a>
### Correspondence

Well-foundedness of a strict order, read for dissipative worlds: with dependent choice it is the absence of an infinite descending chain, constructively it is stronger (nLab, "well-founded relation"). Termination by a potential in a well-founded set is Floyd's (1967) method, after Turing (1949), and its completeness is the classical form of the converse here. A least fall in Archimedean amounts is the discrete case of Hölder's (1901) theorem; the layered amounts are the lexicographic order, the standard non-Archimedean example. Reading (the AI's): what the whole numbers carry in the rest family is one property of the amounts, that nothing in them falls without end.

  - Output: A family's total does not rise and falls strictly at every change of a level.
  - Input: The family's rest is exactly its total's.
  - Preserved conditions: Balance and dissipation from T on. [InAmounts.lean](../../../../experiments/integrated-correction/general-framework/generative-basis/lean/becoming/Becoming/InAmounts.lean)
- **formal-reuse**: [least-loss-rest](least-loss-rest.md). Uses the least-loss law of rest with the falls themselves as the steps counted, and the dyadic and layered amounts as witnesses.
  - Output: Steps losing at least ε from a stock within finitely many ε do not recur.
  - Input: A least fall in Archimedean amounts leaves no endless fall.
  - Preserved conditions: A least fall above nothing; the Archimedean property. [Amounts.lean](../../../../experiments/integrated-correction/general-framework/generative-basis/lean/becoming/Becoming/Amounts.lean)
- related, not a proved adapter: [rest-theorem-in-any-amounts](rest-theorem-in-any-amounts.md). There the rest theorem over any amounts read finitely; here its one premise, exactly.
